purpose: A bounded method for standing up the legal and commercial foundation of a life insurance practice: establishing and maintaining the authority to solicit as jurisdiction-specific requirement classes rather than memorized rules (resident and nonresident licensing, per-carrier per-state appointments, and the recurring obligations that keep both in force); choosing between captive, independent and IMO-affiliated operation on the contract terms that actually decide who owns the book, what a release costs and how contract level silently prices the support that comes with it; reading carrier compensation schedules as mechanisms rather than headline percentages; assembling the smallest product shelf that honestly covers the chosen market's needs from carriers vetted on financial strength, underwriting appetite and service reality; selecting a market focus among families, business owners and the final-expense senior market and testing it against unit economics measured in the practice's own numbers; and building lead generation on disclosure-first contact, evidenced consent, vulnerable-consumer protection and custodial handling of prospect information, so that no prospect is ever contacted before the practice is provably licensed, appointed and ready to serve them.
assumptions: no observed dataset supplied; all scores are heuristic priors

the operator is an individual producer (or a very small agency) building a personal book of life business, not a carrier employee, an agency recruiter running a downline, or a registered investment adviser

licensing, appointment, continuing-education, advertising, do-not-call, replacement and privacy requirements differ by state, by carrier and by channel and change over time, so every such point is named here as an obligation class whose current specifics must be verified with the relevant insurance department, carrier and counsel before acting

compensation, contract level, override, lead cost, close rate, case size and break-even are treated as mechanisms computed from the operator's own carrier schedules, contracts and measured results; no figure in this knowledge base is asserted as a market fact
the durable asset of the practice is a persistent, well-served book, so every foundation decision is judged on what it does to the book over years rather than on first-year cash

cash-value and dividend-paying products are described only by how their mechanics work; illustrations are projections built on stated assumptions and are never treated as promises of future performance
exclusions: fact-finding and needs analysis, term-versus-permanent product mechanics, matching a product to a specific client's need under suitability and best-interest standards, the application, underwriting and policy-delivery process, honest illustration handling and replacement discipline for a live case - that is the needs analysis, product fit and suitability knowledge base this one hands off to

persistency as the economic engine, chargeback, renewal and trail administration over the life of the book, the in-force service cadence that keeps policies from lapsing, policy reviews and life-event triggers, the client-referral engine, and how a book compounds rather than churns - that is the persistency, renewals and book building knowledge base

personalized financial, investment, tax, legal or medical advice to any consumer or business owner; this knowledge base is operator education about how a life practice is licensed, affiliated, stocked and focused

any solicitation, quoting, fact-finding or application activity before a producer license and the applicable carrier appointment are in force; nothing here substitutes for the current requirements published by the insurance department of each state involved

state-specific pre-licensing hours, fees, examination content, continuing-education credit counts, renewal cycles, appointment and just-in-time windows, advertising filing duties and do-not-call specifics, which appear only as obligation classes and must be verified against current rules in each jurisdiction

specific commission percentages, override percentages, renewal or trail rates, target-premium ratios, lead prices, close rates, average case sizes or income figures; compensation and acquisition cost appear only as mechanisms to be computed from the operator's own contracts, carrier schedules and measured results

any promise, projection or implication about investment performance, dividend scale, crediting rate or cash-value growth; a product illustration is a projection under stated assumptions and is never presented as a guarantee
recruiting other agents, building a downline agency, and the economics of overrides earned on other producers' production
drafting, interpreting or valuing buy-sell agreements, entity documents, trusts or business valuations, which belong to the client's own attorney, accountant or valuation professional

competency_questions.question: What exactly must be in force before I may say one word to a prospect about a life policy, and how do I prove on any given day that it still is?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRACTICE_SCOPE_CHARTER states what the practice sells and refuses, RESIDENT_LICENSE_PATH gives the licensing requirement classes and the evidence each produces, and CARRIER_APPOINTMENT_AND_CONTRACTING separates the license from the per-carrier per-state appointment and names the register that is checked before each case

competency_questions.question: Which obligations keep my license and appointments alive, who owns each one, and what actually breaks when I miss one?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CONTINUING_OBLIGATIONS_CALENDAR enumerates the recurring obligation classes with their owner, cadence, lead time and evidence artifact, and states the consequence class of a lapse for pending business and in-force compensation

competency_questions.question: When does a case require a license in another state, and how do I decide which states are worth adding?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: NONRESIDENT_FOOTPRINT explains that authority follows where the applicant is solicited and the policy delivered rather than where the agent sits, names the nonresident license and separate appointment as the requirement classes, and gives the add-a-state decision rule with its recurring cost

competency_questions.question: Captive, independent or IMO-affiliated - what does each model really supply, what does each take, and how do I compare two recruiting offers like for like?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: AFFILIATION_MODEL_COMPARISON compares the three structures on product access, cost borne, relationship ownership and exit, and CONTRACT_LEVEL_AND_UPLINE_ECONOMICS shows how support is priced through contract level so two offers can be compared on the same carrier and product

competency_questions.question: If I leave this agency or upline in three years, what happens to my clients, my renewals and my ability to write with those carriers?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BOOK_OWNERSHIP_TERMS names the specific clause classes that decide the answer - vesting, agent-of-record and client-list ownership, release and waiting period, non-solicitation, orphan reassignment, forfeiture and debit-balance triggers - and requires them abstracted in plain language before the first application

competency_questions.question: How does the money on a sale actually come to exist, and how do I verify what I will be paid on a specific product before I recommend it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: COMPENSATION_SCHEDULE_READING enumerates the structural questions a compensation schedule answers (which premium it is computed on, first-year versus renewal, advance versus as-earned, chargeback window, replacement and increase treatment) and requires a per-carrier abstract verified against the current schedule for the specific product rather than a remembered percentage

competency_questions.question: Which carriers belong on my shelf, how few is too few, and how do I know which carrier will treat a given health or lifestyle risk best?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: CARRIER_FINANCIAL_STRENGTH gives the claims-paying assessment classes, UNDERWRITING_APPETITE_MAP gives the shelf-level impairment and program map built from real case outcomes, CARRIER_SERVICE_DUE_DILIGENCE covers the operational half, and PRODUCT_SHELF_CONSTRUCTION fills one need slot at a time with a primary and a backup

competency_questions.question: Which market should this practice actually serve, and how do I test whether that market can support it before I spend a year finding out?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: MARKET_FOCUS_SELECTION contrasts the family, business-owner and final-expense markets on reach, case size, cadence, knowledge demand and compliance burden and states the fit test, and NICHE_UNIT_ECONOMICS models the chain from cost per lead to cash from a placed case using the practice's own measured inputs with a stated persistency assumption

competency_questions.question: What extra duty of care does an older or otherwise vulnerable buyer impose, and which tactics are simply off the table?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: SENIOR_AND_VULNERABLE_CARE lists the capacity and pressure signals, the concrete protections applied when one appears (slow down, plain-language written summary, trusted person present, affordability check against fixed income, teach-back, stop and document), and the prohibited tactics including fear framing, manufactured urgency and implied government affiliation

competency_questions.question: In the business-owner market, where does my work stop and the client's attorney's or accountant's work begin?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: BUSINESS_OWNER_MARKET_BOUNDARIES separates what the agent does (understand the stated need class, quantify from adviser-supplied documents and figures, arrange coverage with correct ownership and beneficiary structure, coordinate the case) from what the agent refuses (drafting or interpreting agreements, opining on tax treatment, valuing the business) and states the written-referral rule

competency_questions.question: Which lead sources fit my market, what does a lead really cost once placement is counted, and what may never be said or implied to obtain one?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: LEAD_SOURCE_ARCHITECTURE describes each source class by its mechanics and requires evaluation on cost per placed case and evidenced consent provenance, and LEAD_GENERATION_ETHICS states the disclosure-first opening and the prohibited framings, inducement and opt-out obligation classes

competency_questions.question: How is prospect and client information handled, where may it live, and who may see it?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PROSPECT_DATA_PRIVACY treats prospect information including health facts as nonpublic personal information under the practice's custody and states the collection, notice, storage, transmission, sharing, retention and incident-response classes plus the separate consent question for marketing use

competency_questions.question: What is the definition of done before this practice solicits anyone, and what forces the whole foundation to be re-examined later?
competency_questions.acceptance_condition: PRACTICE_READINESS_GATE lists the pass conditions and the rule that a failure holds only the affected state, carrier or market segment with the failed condition named, SHELF_REVIEW_AND_CONCENTRATION sets the shelf re-review cadence, triggers and concentration limit, and ADVERTISING_AND_TITLE_COMPLIANCE requires every public asset to carry its approval evidence and review date

glossary.definition: The state-issued authority to transact insurance in a given line, held either as a resident license in the producer's home state or as a nonresident license in another state; it authorizes the person, carries specific lines of authority such as life, and has an effective and expiration date that the practice tracks.

A carrier's separate filing that authorizes a licensed producer to solicit and submit business for that carrier in a specific state; a license alone never authorizes selling a particular carrier's product, and appointment status is per carrier and per state.

The class of state rules under which a carrier may file the appointment at or shortly after the first application rather than before solicitation; whether it applies, and within what window, varies by state and carrier and must be verified before an application is taken.

An independent (or field) marketing organization that aggregates producers to hold carrier contracts and supplies contracting, case management, training, technology and sometimes leads, taking a share of the compensation stream through the hierarchy and often attaching movement restrictions.

The position on a carrier's or organization's compensation grid assigned to a writing producer, determining how much of the carrier's total compensation on a policy reaches that producer and how much flows upward as overrides; it is the mechanism through which bundled support is actually priced.

The written consent from a current upline or agency allowing a producer to move a carrier contract to a different hierarchy; where a release is withheld, a waiting period defined in the contract typically governs, which is why release terms are read before signing.

The contractual condition under which renewal or trail compensation continues to be paid to the producer after the producing relationship ends, including whether it vests at all, after what period, and whether it survives termination for cause.

Two payment mechanisms for first-year compensation: an advance pays a portion of expected first-year compensation up front and creates a repayable balance if premium is not paid as assumed, while as-earned pays only as premium is received; the choice changes cash-flow timing and chargeback exposure, not the total earned.

A negative balance on the producer's account with a carrier or organization created by advanced compensation that was charged back, unpaid lead or service charges, or other deductions; it can follow a producer between organizations through industry databases and can block new contracting.

A shelf-level map of how each carrier tends to treat recurring impairment, lifestyle and program classes such as build, tobacco use, diabetes, cardiac history, occupation, avocation or accelerated no-exam eligibility; it is compiled from actual case outcomes and current underwriting guides and is used to route a case to the right carrier, not to underwrite it.

nodes.definition: Write down, before any prospect contact, what this practice sells, what it refuses to do, and the exact sentence used when a request falls outside that line. A life practice sells life insurance products under an active producer license and carrier appointments; it educates a household or a business owner about how coverage works and recommends products under the applicable suitability and best-interest standard. It does not give personalized investment, tax, legal or medical advice, does not promise investment performance or guaranteed cash-value growth, and does not solicit in a state or for a carrier where the authority is not in force. The charter names the product classes actually offered, the referral partners for out-of-scope questions (the client's attorney, accountant or investment adviser), and the standing language that an illustration is a projection built on stated assumptions rather than a guarantee. It exists because scope collapses fastest in the moments when a client asks a flattering question and the honest answer is a referral.

included: the product classes the practice offers and the categories it declines
the referral protocol and named partner class for tax, legal, investment and medical questions
the standing no-guarantee and educational-scope language every asset and conversation carries
excluded: the case-level suitability recommendation and its documentation, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base
in-force service promises and retention commitments, which belong to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the practice adds a product class, market or state, or a compliance source restates what a producer may claim

pros.claim: A written refusal list converts the hardest live moments into a rehearsed sentence instead of an improvisation under social pressure
pros.example: a business owner asking the agent to confirm whether premiums on a buy-sell policy are deductible gets the referral sentence rather than an opinion the agent is not licensed to give

cons.claim: A charter drawn too tightly pushes the practice to decline work a properly licensed agent could legitimately do, costing cases for no compliance benefit
cons.example: refusing every business case outright because the charter never separated arranging coverage that funds an agreement from drafting the agreement itself

failure_modes: scope that lives only in the agent's head and therefore moves whenever a large case pushes on it
marketing copy that implies financial-planning or advisory authority the producer license does not carry
answering a tax or legal question conversationally because refusing feels unhelpful
acceptance_tests: the charter names the offered product classes, at least one refusal category with the professional it is referred to, and the no-guarantee sentence, and every public marketing asset and script matches it word for word
revisit_triggers: a new product class, market segment or state is added to the practice
a regulator, carrier or errors-and-omissions carrier restates what a producer may claim or say

nodes.definition: Treat becoming licensed as a sequence of requirement classes rather than a memorized checklist, because every specific rule belongs to a state insurance department and changes. The classes that recur: a pre-licensing education requirement in some jurisdictions, a life (or combined life-and-health) line-of-authority examination, an application with a fee, a background and fingerprint requirement, a resident-state determination that fixes which department is the home regulator, and in some places a sponsorship, character-reference or bonding condition. The work is to identify which classes the state imposes today and in what order, know what evidence artifact each produces (a course completion certificate, an exam score report, a license number with effective and expiration dates), and verify each against the department's current published requirements rather than a recruiter's summary or another candidate's experience. Licensing is the hard precondition for everything else in this knowledge base: without it there is no lawful conversation to have.

included: identifying which requirement classes the resident state imposes and their order
collecting and filing the evidence artifact each class produces
confirming the line of authority and the resident-state determination
excluded: state-specific hour counts, fees, exam content and passing scores, which must be read from the department's current publication
carrier appointment, which is a separate authority obtained per carrier and per state

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: the resident state changes a licensing requirement class or the producer's state of residence changes

pros.claim: Holding the path as classes rather than a fixed list keeps the plan correct when a state changes hours, vendors or fees
pros.example: a state moves to a new fingerprint vendor and only the evidence artifact for the background class changes, not the sequence or the timeline

cons.claim: Class-level knowledge cannot answer the concrete question a candidate has today, so every step still requires a jurisdiction lookup before acting
cons.example: the candidate still has to read the department's current bulletin to learn how many pre-licensing hours to book and whether the exam vendor changed

failure_modes: assuming a neighbouring state's or a prior cohort's requirements still apply
letting a recruiter's start-date timeline drive activity before the background class clears
sitting the exam for the wrong line of authority for the intended market
acceptance_tests: the license record shows the life line of authority active with its number and expiration date, and every requirement class in the state's current publication is matched to a filed evidence artifact
revisit_triggers: the department publishes changed pre-licensing, examination, fee or background requirements
the producer's state of residence changes, which moves the home-state determination

nodes.definition: Decide deliberately which states the practice is licensed in, because the authority that matters generally follows where the applicant is located when solicited and where the policy is delivered, not where the agent happens to sit. The requirement classes are a nonresident license in each such state, commonly obtainable on the strength of the resident license through a reciprocity process, plus a separate carrier appointment in that state for each carrier used there. Footprint is a business decision carrying a recurring cost: each added state adds a renewal, potentially its own continuing-education or reporting conditions, and another set of advertising, replacement and disclosure rules to keep straight. The discipline is to add a state because the chosen market genuinely straddles a border, a referral pattern repeats, or a carrier requires it - never speculatively, and never after a case has already appeared - and to verify current nonresident and appointment requirements with that state's department before soliciting anyone there.

included: the rule class that ties authority to where the applicant is solicited and the policy delivered
the nonresident license and matching per-state appointment as separate requirements
the deliberate add-a-state decision rule and its recurring maintenance cost
excluded: the specific reciprocity mechanics, fees and renewal cycles of any named state, which are verified with that department
situs determinations for unusual fact patterns, which are carrier and compliance questions rather than field decisions

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a repeated case flow appears from an unlicensed state or a state changes nonresident licensing requirements

pros.claim: A deliberate footprint keeps renewal, education and rule-tracking load proportional to where business actually comes from
pros.example: an agent whose market is one metropolitan area spanning a state line carries two licenses instead of a speculative dozen and still covers every case that appears

cons.claim: A narrow footprint means real cases arrive that cannot be written, and the licensing lead time is too long to solve them in the moment
cons.example: a client relocates mid-application to a state the agent is not licensed in, and the case must be referred out or paused until authority exists

failure_modes: soliciting a prospect who has moved without checking which state's authority the case now needs
collecting nonresident licenses speculatively and then missing a renewal on one that produced nothing
holding a nonresident license but forgetting the separate carrier appointment in that state
acceptance_tests: every state in the footprint has a documented business reason, an active license, the intended carrier appointments confirmed for that state, and its renewal and education obligations added to the compliance calendar
revisit_triggers: a referral pattern or repeated case flow appears from an unlicensed state
a state changes its nonresident or reciprocity requirements, or a licensed state produces no business through a full renewal cycle

nodes.definition: A license permits a person to transact insurance; a carrier appointment is the separate authority to solicit and submit business for that specific carrier in that specific state, and both must be in force at the moment of solicitation. Contracting is effectively an underwriting of the agent: a packet carrying licensing evidence, errors-and-omissions coverage, background and disclosure questions, and in most cases a check against industry databases that surface prior terminations, complaints and unpaid agent balances, so an old debit balance or an undisclosed termination can block a contract months after the fact. States differ on whether an appointment must be filed before the first application or may be filed just-in-time within a defined window after it, and carriers differ on whether they will do so, which means that rule is verified per carrier and per state before a first application is taken there. The output is a per-carrier, per-state authority register with effective and termination dates, checked before every case rather than remembered.

included: the contracting packet and the agent-underwriting checks it triggers
appointment as per-carrier, per-state authority with effective and termination dates
the just-in-time versus pre-appointment rule class verified per carrier and state
the authority register consulted before each case
excluded: the compensation terms inside the same contract, which are read as their own work unit
ownership, vesting and release clauses, which are abstracted separately before signing

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an appointment is added or terminated, or a carrier or state changes its pre-appointment and just-in-time rules

pros.claim: An authority register with dates makes the pre-case check a lookup rather than a memory exercise across many carriers and states
pros.example: before a cross-border case the agent confirms in one place that the carrier is appointed in that state and the appointment has not been terminated for inactivity

cons.claim: Contracting is slow and front-loaded, so the register is stale exactly when a new opportunity arrives and appointments take time to add
cons.example: a referral for a product only one uncontracted carrier writes well arrives with no time to complete contracting before the client's need date

failure_modes: assuming a license alone permits writing a given carrier's product
omitting a prior termination or unresolved balance on the contracting disclosure and having the contract voided later
letting an appointment terminate for inactivity and discovering it only when an application is rejected
acceptance_tests: for every carrier and state the practice intends to write in, the register shows an in-force appointment or a verified just-in-time rule with its window, and errors-and-omissions coverage is evidenced and current
revisit_triggers: a carrier terminates or does not renew an appointment, including for inactivity
the practice adds a state or a carrier, or an affiliation change requires contracts to be re-papered through a different hierarchy

nodes.definition: Licensing is not an event but a set of recurring obligation classes that expire quietly and stop the practice when they do. The classes to calendar: continuing-education credits including any ethics component, license renewal on each state's own cycle, carrier-required training such as anti-money-laundering and product-specific certifications, errors-and-omissions coverage renewal, notification duties when an address, legal name or business affiliation changes, reporting duties when an administrative action, complaint or criminal charge occurs, and any subscription or list obligations that support lawful contact. Each class is recorded with its owner (state department, carrier, marketing organization, errors-and-omissions carrier), its cadence, a lead time long enough to actually complete it, and the evidence artifact it produces. The consequence of missing one is not merely a fee: an expired license or lapsed appointment can stop pending business and, depending on the applicable rule, affect compensation on business written while authority was out of force, which is why the calendar is built the day the first license is issued.

included: the recurring obligation classes with owner, cadence, lead time and evidence artifact
the consequence class of a lapse for pending business and compensation
one calendar covering every state in the footprint and every contracted carrier
excluded: the specific credit counts, cycles and fees of any named state, verified with that department
the in-force policy service cadence owed to clients, which belongs to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a state or carrier changes a continuing obligation, or the licensed footprint or carrier list changes

pros.claim: A single calendar with lead times turns a scattered set of expiries into routine work done before anything is at risk
pros.example: the continuing-education block is booked a full cycle ahead of the renewal date, so a full pipeline is never paused by a course that could not be scheduled in time

cons.claim: Maintaining the calendar is unglamorous overhead that competes directly with selling time and is the first thing dropped in a busy month
cons.example: the annual carrier certification is postponed through a strong quarter and blocks new submissions with that carrier at the worst moment

failure_modes: tracking only the resident license and missing a nonresident state's separate cycle
treating carrier-required training as optional until a submission is blocked
failing to report an address change or administrative action within the required window
acceptance_tests: every obligation class for every licensed state and contracted carrier appears with an owner, a due date, a lead-time reminder and a completed-evidence field, and no item is past due
revisit_triggers: a state or carrier changes a continuing-education, training or reporting requirement
a state or carrier is added to or removed from the practice

nodes.definition: Everything the practice publishes to attract a prospect is an insurance advertisement in the regulatory sense, and it passes through two overlapping approval layers: the carrier's advertising review for anything naming its products, name or marks, and the state's rules on what an insurance advertisement may claim, how the producer must be identified, and whether the piece must be filed or retained. The recurring failure classes are using a carrier's name, logo or product illustration without written approval; titles, designations or role descriptions that imply an advisory capacity, a government affiliation, or an expertise the producer does not hold; and content implying guaranteed returns, free benefits or an entitlement. The operating artifact is one reviewed asset library - website pages, social profiles and posts, mailers, seminar decks, business cards, email signatures, video - each entry carrying its approval evidence and review date, with a standing rule that nothing new goes public until it has cleared the same path.

included: the carrier-approval and state-rule layers over any prospect-facing asset
title, designation and affiliation claim discipline
the reviewed asset library with approval evidence and review dates
excluded: the specific filing and retention rules of any named state, which are verified with that department
the content of a case-specific illustration presented to a client, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier or state changes advertising review rules, or the practice adds a channel or public designation

pros.claim: A reviewed asset library makes compliant marketing repeatable and survives an audit or complaint because the approval trail already exists
pros.example: when a carrier asks how its product was described in a mailer, the exact approved version and its approval date are produced in minutes

cons.claim: Approval cycles are slow and blunt the timeliness that makes some channels work at all
cons.example: a topical social post loses its moment while it waits in a carrier review queue, pushing the agent toward generic evergreen content

failure_modes: posting carrier logos or product specifics without written approval because a colleague did it first
using a title or designation that implies advisory or government status
letting an approved piece drift through small edits until it no longer matches what was approved
acceptance_tests: every live prospect-facing asset appears in the library with its approval evidence, review date and the exact approved wording, and no asset claims a guarantee, an entitlement or an unheld designation
revisit_triggers: a carrier updates its advertising rules or withdraws approval for a piece
the practice adds a channel, a state, or a designation to its public identity

nodes.definition: Compare the three structures the practice can operate under on what each supplies and what each takes, because the choice sets product access, cost structure and exit terms for years. A captive career agency typically supplies structured training, office and administrative infrastructure, a defined product line, mentoring and sometimes an early-period subsidy, and takes product breadth, a share of control over the client relationship, and often the freedom to place a case with an outside carrier. Fully independent operation supplies product freedom and direct carrier contracts and takes on the entire cost of leads, technology, errors-and-omissions coverage, compliance administration and back office, plus the burden of meeting each carrier's own production conditions. IMO or FMO affiliation sits between: the organization aggregates producers to hold carrier contracts and supplies contracting, case management, underwriting advocacy, training, technology and sometimes leads, taking a share of compensation through the hierarchy and frequently attaching movement restrictions. The decision is made on four durable axes - who owns the client relationship, what happens to compensation if the affiliation ends, what the support is actually worth against its real price, and whether product access matches the chosen market - not on the size of a first-year bonus.

included: the captive, independent and IMO-affiliated structures compared on supply, cost, ownership and exit
the four durable decision axes
like-for-like comparison of two recruiting offers
excluded: the specific clause language that decides ownership and release, which is abstracted in its own work unit
recruiting other producers and building a downline, which this knowledge base excludes entirely

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an organization changes support, contract level or release policy, or the chosen market outgrows the model's product access

pros.claim: Judging the model on ownership, exit, real support price and product access exposes offers whose headline attraction is funded by terms that bind for years
pros.example: a generous training package turns out to be conditioned on a multi-year exclusivity that would prevent placing final-expense cases with the carriers that write them best

cons.claim: The comparison is made with the least information the agent will ever have, and the model that suits a beginner is often not the one that suits an established producer
cons.example: a new agent correctly chooses a captive structure for training, then spends a year and a release period unwinding it once independent product access matters more

failure_modes: choosing on a recruiting presentation's income projection rather than on contract terms
treating training and leads as free because no invoice is issued for them
signing with multiple organizations for the same carrier and creating hierarchy conflicts that block contracting
acceptance_tests: the decision memo scores each candidate model on product access for the chosen market, total cost borne including support priced through contract level, client-relationship ownership, and the exit path with its waiting period
revisit_triggers: the chosen market changes and the current model cannot supply a carrier for a need slot
the organization changes its support, contract level, production conditions or release policy

nodes.definition: Find and abstract the clauses that decide who owns the durable asset, because they are the difference between building a book and renting one. The clause classes to read before signing: whether renewal or trail compensation is vested, after what period, and whether vesting survives termination generally or only termination without cause; who is contractually the agent of record and whether the client list and its data belong to the producer, the agency or the carrier; what a release requires if the producer wants to move carrier contracts to another hierarchy, who may withhold it, and what waiting period applies when it is withheld; non-solicitation and confidentiality restrictions that may limit contacting the producer's own past clients after departure; how orphaned policies are reassigned when a producer leaves; and the forfeiture triggers, including termination for cause and an unpaid debit balance. These terms are almost never renegotiated after the fact and are frequently different from what was described verbally, so they are abstracted into plain language, compared across offers, and accepted knowingly before the first application is written under that contract.

included: vesting, agent-of-record and client-list ownership, release and waiting period, non-solicitation, orphan reassignment, forfeiture and debit-balance clauses
a plain-language abstract compared across competing offers
the rule that terms are accepted before the first application under that contract
excluded: legal advice on enforceability, which belongs to the producer's own attorney
the ongoing servicing and retention of the book, which belongs to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an agent agreement or compensation addendum is amended, or a hierarchy move is contemplated

pros.claim: A plain-language abstract makes the exit cost visible while it can still influence the decision, which is the only moment it can
pros.example: the abstract shows that renewals vest only after a stated period and are forfeited on termination for cause, changing which of two offers is actually worth more over a decade

cons.claim: Insisting on reading and questioning terms slows onboarding and can be read as distrust by an organization eager to get the agent producing
cons.example: a recruiter treats a written question about release conditions as a lack of commitment, and the agent must hold the line anyway

failure_modes: relying on a verbal assurance that release is never withheld in practice
discovering a non-solicitation restriction only after leaving, when the client list is already unusable
signing multiple contracts whose terms conflict about who owns the same client relationship
acceptance_tests: a plain-language abstract exists for each signed or candidate contract covering vesting, ownership, release and waiting period, non-solicitation, orphan handling and forfeiture triggers, with the source clause referenced for each line
revisit_triggers: the organization or carrier amends its agent agreement or compensation addendum
the producer contemplates moving hierarchies, adding a second organization, or is offered a new contract level

nodes.definition: Understand the hierarchy as a mechanism rather than a ladder of status. A carrier pays a total compensation amount on a policy; the contract level assigned to the writing producer determines how much of that total reaches the producer, and the remainder flows upward as overrides to the uplines that hold the contract. This is why free leads, a free customer system, training, mentoring, case design help and office space are never free: they are funded by a lower contract level, by a lead or service charge deducted from compensation, by a production commitment, or by some combination the recruiting conversation may not itemize. The evaluation is therefore a like-for-like comparison on the same carrier and the same product: what level is offered, what services come with it, what those same services would cost if bought directly, and what conditions ride along - production minimums, exclusivity, movement restrictions, chargeback of lead costs. A higher level with no support can be worth less than a lower level with genuine underwriting advocacy and case design; the only way to know is to price both sides instead of comparing headline levels.

included: the override mechanism and how contract level splits a carrier's total compensation
the true price of bundled leads, technology, training and case support
like-for-like comparison of two offers on one carrier and product with conditions attached
excluded: specific level percentages or override figures, which are read from the actual contract and vary by carrier, product and organization
earning overrides on other producers' business, which this knowledge base excludes

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: an organization changes contract levels, lead charges or production conditions, or production qualifies the producer for a different level

pros.claim: Pricing the support explicitly turns an emotional recruiting comparison into an arithmetic one the producer can actually check
pros.example: the value of supplied leads and case management is estimated at their direct purchase cost and set against the level difference on the same product, revealing which offer is genuinely better

cons.claim: The comparison depends on estimating the worth of support that has no invoice, so it stays partly subjective and can be gamed by an organization that emphasizes whichever side flatters it
cons.example: mentoring quality cannot be priced honestly before experiencing it, and a strong mentor is worth far more than the level difference while a weak one is worth nothing

failure_modes: chasing the highest advertised level without checking what support disappears at that level
accepting bundled leads whose cost is charged back against future compensation without modelling the exposure
signing a production condition that forces volume the chosen market cannot honestly produce
acceptance_tests: for each offer, one carrier and product is priced at the offered level with the bundled services valued at their direct cost and every attached condition listed, and the comparison is recorded before signing
revisit_triggers: the organization changes contract levels, lead charges or production conditions
actual production makes a different level or a direct contract available

nodes.definition: Read the compensation schedule as the document that defines how money comes to exist on each product, before recommending anything from that shelf. The structural questions it answers: which premium the compensation is computed on, since for many permanent products a target-versus-excess split changes the answer entirely; how first-year compensation differs from renewal and service compensation and for how many years each runs; whether first-year compensation is advanced against expected premium or paid as earned; what the chargeback rule is if the policy lapses, is surrendered, is not taken or is rescinded inside the chargeback window, and whether it is a full or graded chargeback; how the carrier treats internal replacements, exchanges, term conversions, face-amount increases and riders; and what happens to compensation on business written while an appointment was not in force. Because these mechanics differ by product, by state, by issue age and by contract level, a percentage learned from one contract predicts nothing about another. The practice keeps a per-carrier abstract of the mechanisms and verifies the current schedule for the specific product before quoting it.

included: the structural questions a compensation schedule answers for any product
advance versus as-earned mechanics and the chargeback window as exposure classes
a per-carrier abstract verified against the current schedule before quoting
excluded: stating or implying any specific percentage, which must be read from the operator's own current schedule
managing chargeback exposure and renewal income over the life of the book, which belongs to the persistency knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier reissues a compensation schedule, or the contract level or product set changes

pros.claim: Knowing the mechanism rather than a number keeps the practice correct across carriers, products and contract changes and prevents cash-flow surprises
pros.example: recognizing that compensation on a permanent product follows the target-premium split explains why two similar-looking cases pay very differently and why funding design matters

cons.claim: Schedules are long, product-specific and frequently amended, so keeping abstracts current is real recurring work that never feels urgent
cons.example: a carrier reissues its schedule with a changed chargeback window and the practice's abstract silently goes stale until a chargeback arrives

failure_modes: quoting a product on a remembered percentage from a different carrier or a different contract level
treating an advance as earned income and being unprepared for the repayment obligation when a policy lapses early
ignoring how the schedule treats replacements and exchanges until a case triggers the clause
acceptance_tests: each shelf product has a dated abstract naming the premium basis, first-year and renewal structure, advance or as-earned mechanism, chargeback window and rule, and replacement or exchange treatment, sourced from the current schedule
revisit_triggers: a carrier reissues or amends a compensation schedule
the producer's contract level changes or a new product is added to the shelf

nodes.definition: A life policy is a promise that may be called decades from now, so the carrier's ability and willingness to pay is part of the recommendation rather than a footnote. The assessment classes: independent rating-agency opinions, which are opinions about relative claims-paying ability rather than guarantees and which use different scales that must be read on their own terms rather than compared letter to letter; the carrier's ownership form, mutual or stock, and what it implies for how surplus, dividends and long-term policyholder interests are treated; the age, size and concentration of its in-force book and its reinsurance posture; its historical behaviour toward existing policyholders, including cost-of-insurance adjustments, dividend-scale changes and service continuity through acquisitions; and the state guaranty association framework, which exists as a backstop with limits that vary by state and may never be presented to a client as a reason to disregard carrier quality or as a marketing point. The practice records why each shelf carrier was accepted on these grounds, with the date and the source consulted, and re-checks when ratings, ownership or in-force behaviour change.

included: rating-agency opinions as opinions, read on each agency's own scale
ownership form, in-force behaviour and treatment of existing policyholders
the guaranty framework as a backstop that is never a selling point
excluded: predicting any carrier's future solvency or performance
explaining or projecting policy values to a client, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a rating, outlook, ownership or in-force treatment change is reported at a shelf carrier

pros.claim: Weighing durability alongside price protects the client on the only dimension that matters at claim time and protects the agent's own book from a carrier that mistreats in-force policyholders
pros.example: a carrier with a pattern of increasing cost-of-insurance charges on in-force blocks is passed over despite an attractive current rate

cons.claim: Strength assessments are backward-looking opinions and can screen out perfectly sound carriers whose current pricing would serve clients better
cons.example: a smaller regional carrier with limited rating coverage but sound fundamentals is excluded by a mechanical rating cutoff

failure_modes: treating a rating as a guarantee or comparing letter grades across agencies with different scales
using guaranty association coverage as a reassurance in a sales conversation
choosing purely on current rate for a promise that must last decades
acceptance_tests: each shelf carrier has a dated acceptance record naming the ratings consulted with their agency and scale, the ownership form, any known in-force behaviour concerns, and the reason it was accepted
revisit_triggers: a rating change, outlook change, acquisition or ownership change at a shelf carrier
a reported change in a carrier's treatment of in-force policyholders such as a cost-of-insurance or dividend-scale adjustment

nodes.definition: Maintain a shelf-level map of which carriers treat which risk profiles well, because on identical health and lifestyle facts different carriers reach materially different offers. The map is organized around the classes that recur in the chosen market: tobacco and nicotine-substitute use, build charts, controlled versus uncontrolled diabetes, cardiac and cancer history by time since event, mental-health and substance-use history, prescription-history patterns, hazardous occupations and avocations, aviation, foreign travel or foreign nationality, driving and criminal history, and family history. It also records program-level facts: which carriers offer accelerated or fluidless underwriting and up to what age and face-amount class, which are pragmatic about table credits, and which are workable across the final-expense tiers from full underwriting through simplified issue to guaranteed issue with its graded-benefit class. The map is built from actual case outcomes and current underwriting guides rather than reputation, and it is a routing and shelf-selection tool only: the case-level fact-find, informal inquiry, offer negotiation and delivery of a rated offer belong to the needs analysis and underwriting knowledge base.

included: shelf-level appetite by recurring impairment, lifestyle and occupation class
program-level facts such as accelerated underwriting eligibility and final-expense tiering
compilation from real case outcomes and current underwriting guides
excluded: the case-level fact-find, informal inquiry, requirement gathering and offer negotiation, which belong to the needs analysis knowledge base
any medical judgement about a client's condition or prognosis

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier revises an underwriting guide or program, or observed case outcomes contradict a mapped entry

pros.claim: Routing a risk to the carrier that treats it best raises placement and shortens cycle time without changing anything about the client
pros.example: a well-controlled diabetic applicant is routed to the shelf carrier whose published guide treats that class most favourably instead of being submitted where a rating is near certain

cons.claim: Appetite drifts continuously as carriers reprice and revise guides, so a map built once becomes quietly wrong and misroutes cases with confidence
cons.example: a carrier tightens its build chart after a repricing and the map keeps sending those cases there until several rate-ups reveal the change

failure_modes: building the map from agent folklore rather than current guides and actual outcomes
letting the map harden into a habit of always submitting to one carrier
using appetite knowledge to coach an applicant toward an inaccurate answer, which is misrepresentation rather than routing
acceptance_tests: the map covers the impairment and program classes that recur in the chosen market, each entry cites the underwriting guide version or the case outcomes behind it, and each entry carries a last-reviewed date
revisit_triggers: a carrier revises an underwriting guide, program eligibility or build chart
a pattern of unexpected ratings, declines or requirement escalations appears in one risk class

nodes.definition: Build the smallest shelf that can honestly serve the chosen market, then stop adding to it. The design question is coverage of need classes, not the number of carrier contracts held. For a family market that generally means a competitive term line with genuinely useful conversion privileges, at least one permanent chassis for the needs term cannot serve, and a simplified-issue path for applicants who will not complete an exam. For a final-expense market it means small-face whole life across the underwriting tiers, including a guaranteed-issue option with its graded-benefit mechanics understood well enough to explain plainly. For a business-owner market it means carriers whose underwriting, case support and administration handle larger faces, third-party ownership and multi-life structures. Each slot on the shelf names the need class it exists to fill, a primary and one backup carrier, and the reason both are there. A shelf spread too wide costs certification time, appointment maintenance, product knowledge depth and per-carrier production minimums; a shelf too narrow forces the agent to fit the client to the product, which is the specific failure the whole practice is built to prevent.

included: one shelf slot per need class the chosen market presents, each with a primary and a backup carrier
the deliberate limit on shelf width and its stated cost
the written reason each carrier occupies its slot
excluded: choosing between term and permanent for an individual client and documenting that suitability, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base
product mechanics explained to a client, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a shelf product is discontinued or repriced, or the market presents a need class with no slot

pros.claim: A need-slot shelf with a named backup means every case the chosen market presents has somewhere honest to go, including when the primary carrier declines
pros.example: a term applicant who returns a rated offer moves to the mapped backup rather than being talked into whatever the single contracted carrier will issue

cons.claim: Every additional carrier costs contracting, certification, product study and possibly a production minimum, so breadth bought for rare cases degrades depth on common ones
cons.example: carrying a specialist carrier for occasional foreign-national cases means annual certifications and a minimum that the case flow never justifies

failure_modes: collecting carrier contracts as a status signal rather than filling need slots
leaving a need class the chosen market genuinely presents with no shelf slot at all
reshaping the client's stated need to fit the product the shelf happens to carry
acceptance_tests: every need class the chosen market presents has a slot with a named primary and backup carrier, a written reason, and confirmed appointment status, and each carrier on the shelf fills at least one slot
revisit_triggers: a shelf product is discontinued, repriced or has its underwriting class structure changed
the market focus changes, or repeated cases arrive for a need class with no slot

nodes.definition: Judge each candidate carrier on the operational half that decides whether business actually gets placed and stays placed. The dimensions to test: the electronic application and which states and products it covers; illustration software quality, licensing and whether it can be run without a support call; underwriting turnaround and how requirements and decisions are communicated; whether a responsive agent support desk and a named case manager exist; policy-delivery requirements and how delivery receipts are handled; the service experience the client will actually live with, including billing and draft options, beneficiary and address changes, the service portal, and the carrier's reputation at claim time; and the clarity, timeliness and disputability of compensation statements. A carrier with an attractive rate and a broken service experience produces not-taken policies, avoidable early lapses and complaints that land on the agent rather than the carrier. This diligence is done by live testing - running a quote end to end, submitting a permitted test case, calling the support line and timing the answer - rather than by reading marketing material or trusting a recruiter's characterization.

included: electronic application, illustration tooling, underwriting turnaround and support responsiveness
the policyholder service and claims experience the client will live with
compensation statement clarity and dispute path
live testing rather than marketing claims
excluded: case-level underwriting negotiation and requirement chasing, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base
the ongoing in-force service cadence the agent owes the client, which belongs to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a carrier acquisition or platform change occurs, or placed-client service complaints cluster at one carrier

pros.claim: Testing service before contracting prevents a whole class of avoidable losses that surface only after clients are already placed with the carrier
pros.example: a trial submission exposes an electronic application that cannot handle a common ownership structure in the target market, disqualifying the carrier before any client is exposed to it

cons.claim: Service quality is sampled at one moment and changes with staffing, system migrations and acquisitions, so today's test does not guarantee tomorrow's experience
cons.example: a carrier acquired the following year migrates its service platform and turnaround degrades across the board

failure_modes: selecting on rate alone and absorbing the service cost as unexplained not-taken policies
testing only the sales tools and never the policyholder-facing service the client will use for decades
ignoring unclear or untimely compensation statements until a payment dispute arises
acceptance_tests: each shelf carrier has a dated diligence record covering application tooling, underwriting turnaround, support responsiveness, policyholder service and statement clarity, with the observation behind each rating noted
revisit_triggers: a carrier acquisition, platform migration or service reorganization
a pattern of delivery delays, service complaints or statement disputes from placed clients

nodes.definition: Treat the shelf as a portfolio that is re-reviewed on a cadence and on events, and set an explicit limit on how much of the practice's in-force business and expected income may depend on a single carrier or a single upline. The trigger events: a product discontinued, repriced or restructured; an underwriting class or program change; a rating, outlook or ownership change; a service degradation; a change to the compensation schedule or the agent agreement; or a production minimum the practice will not realistically meet. The review asks three questions each time: is each need slot still filled by the right primary and backup, has anything changed that would make a recommendation pattern look different for new clients going forward, and is the practice now too dependent on one relationship that could be terminated or repriced unilaterally. The output is a dated review record and, where a change is needed, a replacement carrier contracted and appointed before the incumbent is dropped, so no slot is ever empty while cases are arriving.

included: the review cadence and its trigger events
the concentration limit across carriers and uplines
the replace-before-drop sequencing rule and the dated review record
excluded: revisiting or replacing an individual client's existing policy, which is replacement discipline in the needs analysis knowledge base
in-force block servicing and retention, which belongs to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a trigger event fires at a shelf carrier or the in-force distribution crosses the concentration limit

pros.claim: A cadence plus explicit triggers catches shelf decay early, while a concentration limit keeps a single carrier or upline decision from being able to halt the practice
pros.example: when a primary carrier withdraws a product mid-year the backup is already contracted, so cases keep flowing while the slot is refilled

cons.claim: Deliberate diversification costs depth, certifications and production credit that a concentrated practice converts into better levels and better service
cons.example: spreading business across two carriers keeps the practice below the production threshold that would have earned stronger support at one

failure_modes: reviewing only when something has already broken
dropping a carrier before its replacement is contracted and appointed, leaving a need slot empty
allowing one upline relationship to hold every contract, so a single dispute freezes the whole practice
acceptance_tests: a dated review record exists for the current cycle covering every slot, and no single carrier or upline exceeds the written concentration limit without a documented mitigation
revisit_triggers: any trigger event fires at a shelf carrier, including product, rating, ownership, service or compensation changes
the practice's in-force distribution crosses the concentration limit

nodes.definition: Choose the market the practice serves before choosing carriers, products or leads, because every downstream decision is derived from it. The candidate markets differ on nearly every operating variable. Young families and mortgage-protection buyers are numerous and reachable, buy modest term premiums, and reward volume, speed and a simple repeatable process. Business owners and higher-income households buy larger and structurally more complex cases with long sales cycles, demand real technical partnering with the client's other advisers, and put the agent in competition with established professionals. The final-expense and senior market is reachable with a simple product and a highly repeatable process, but carries the heaviest duty of care, the strictest scrutiny of contact practices, and buyers whose ability to pay is fixed. The fit test asks five questions honestly: can I reach these people repeatedly through a channel I can afford and sustain, does the case size and cadence support the income the practice needs, do I have or can I realistically build the product and underwriting knowledge this market demands, does its compliance burden match what I can maintain, and would I be content serving these clients for the next ten years. Focus is chosen once, tested with measured results, and changed deliberately rather than drifted out of.

included: the operating differences between the family, business-owner and final-expense markets
the five-question fit test and its honest answers
the rule that focus changes deliberately rather than by drift
excluded: the needs analysis conducted with an individual client inside the chosen market, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base
referral systems built on an existing book, which belong to the book building knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured results miss the modelled economics for consecutive cycles or access to the market changes

pros.claim: One chosen market lets carriers, products, scripts, lead sources and knowledge compound instead of being rebuilt for every case type
pros.example: an agent focused on final expense learns three carriers' simplified-issue question sets deeply enough to field-underwrite accurately on the first call

cons.claim: Focus means declining or referring cases that arrive from outside it, which is expensive early when any case feels necessary
cons.example: a well-connected business-owner referral arrives at a final-expense practice and either goes to a partner or consumes weeks of learning the practice had not budgeted

failure_modes: choosing the market a recruiter's compensation grid favours rather than the one the agent can actually reach
declaring a focus and then working every lead that appears, so nothing compounds
entering the senior market for its accessibility without accepting its duty-of-care burden
acceptance_tests: the market focus is written with each of the five fit-test questions answered from the agent's real access, capacity and knowledge, and the out-of-focus case protocol names where such cases go
revisit_triggers: measured results miss the modelled economics for consecutive cycles
access to the market changes, such as losing a referral channel or an association relationship

nodes.definition: Model the chosen market's economics as a chain of mechanisms populated exclusively with the practice's own measured numbers, never with figures borrowed from a recruiting presentation or an industry claim. The chain runs: cost per lead or per hour of outreach, contact rate, appointment-set rate, appointment-kept rate, application rate, placement rate after underwriting and delivery, average annualized premium per placed case, the compensation mechanism from the carrier's schedule at the producer's actual contract level, and the timing of payment, since an advance changes cash flow rather than profit. Two ratios decide viability: acquisition cost per placed case against first-year compensation per placed case, and the elapsed time from spend to cash. Because early-duration compensation is exposed to chargeback, a model that assumes every placed case stays on the books overstates reality, so the model carries an explicit, labelled persistency assumption that the book-management practice later measures and feeds back. Every input is dated, sourced to how it was measured, and re-measured on a cadence; an input that has never been observed is marked as an assumption rather than promoted to a fact.

included: the measured chain from outreach cost to cash from a placed case
the two viability ratios and the cash-timing distinction
the explicit labelled persistency assumption and the dated re-measurement of every input
excluded: measuring and managing actual persistency, chargebacks and renewal income over the life of the book, which belongs to the persistency knowledge base
any income projection presented to a recruit or a client as achievable

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: measured rates, lead costs or compensation mechanics diverge from the modelled inputs

pros.claim: A chain of measured rates shows exactly which step is breaking, so effort and budget go to the failing stage instead of to more leads
pros.example: a poor placement rate rather than a poor contact rate reveals the problem is carrier routing and field underwriting, which more lead spend would only amplify

cons.claim: Early in a practice the sample is too small for the rates to be stable, so the model can mislead precisely when the decisions it informs are largest
cons.example: two unusually good weeks of appointments set an acquisition-cost expectation that a full quarter does not support

failure_modes: populating the model with figures from a recruiting presentation instead of measured results
treating advanced compensation as profit and building a spending plan on cash that may be charged back
omitting the persistency assumption so the model implies every placed case is permanent income
acceptance_tests: every input in the chain carries a date, a source describing how it was measured or an explicit assumption label, and the model states the persistency assumption and the acquisition-cost-to-first-year-compensation ratio it produces
revisit_triggers: a lead source's cost or quality shifts, or a carrier changes the compensation mechanism
measured placement or persistency diverges from the modelled assumption

nodes.definition: Serving older and otherwise vulnerable buyers imposes a higher standard of care as a first-class operating rule, not a courtesy extended when convenient. The protocol has two halves. First, recognize the signals that a prospect may not be able to evaluate the transaction freely: confusion about basic facts already covered, inability to recall the purpose of the meeting, a third party who answers on their behalf or presses for a decision, evident grief or distress, isolation, or a stated income that cannot absorb the premium being discussed. Second, respond with concrete protections rather than a faster close: slow the process down, use plain language and leave a written summary, invite a trusted family member or the buyer's own adviser to be present, offer a trusted-contact designation where the carrier supports one, check affordability against a fixed income before recommending any premium, ask the buyer to restate in their own words what is being bought and what it costs, and stop entirely and document the reason where capacity is genuinely in question. Fear-based framing, manufactured urgency, implying a government or benefit-program affiliation, exploiting a recent bereavement, and in-home pressure tactics are prohibited regardless of what the market tolerates or what a competitor does.

included: the capacity, isolation, third-party pressure and affordability signals
the concrete protections applied when a signal appears, including stopping and documenting
the prohibited tactic list that applies regardless of market practice
excluded: any clinical or capacity determination, which is a medical and legal judgement the agent never makes
the suitability documentation for the resulting recommendation, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint or early-lapse pattern appears in the senior segment, or conduct expectations are restated by a regulator or carrier

pros.claim: A written protocol makes the protective response automatic at the exact moment commercial pressure argues against it
pros.example: when an adult child answers every question for a parent, the agent pauses the appointment and reschedules with the parent able to participate, rather than closing on the child's answers

cons.claim: Slowing down and involving family costs sales that a faster competitor will take, and some capable older buyers find the extra care patronizing
cons.example: a sharp buyer is mildly offended at being asked to restate the policy terms, while the same step protects the next buyer who could not

failure_modes: treating age itself as incapacity rather than watching for actual signals
closing in the presence of an interested relative whose pressure the buyer cannot resist
recommending a premium a fixed income cannot sustain, guaranteeing an early lapse that harms the buyer most
acceptance_tests: the file for any case showing a vulnerability signal records which signal appeared, which protections were applied, the affordability check against stated income, and the buyer's own restatement of what was purchased
revisit_triggers: a complaint, a family objection, or an early lapse pattern in the senior segment
a regulator, carrier or association updates vulnerable-consumer or senior-market conduct expectations

nodes.definition: The business-owner market pays in larger cases and durable relationships, and it sits directly against the line between insurance work and the practice of law, accounting and investment advice. What belongs to the agent: understanding the owner's stated need class, such as replacing the economic contribution of a key person, funding an obligation created by an existing agreement, satisfying a lender's collateral assignment requirement, or arranging an executive benefit; quantifying the insurance amount from documents and figures that the client's own advisers supply; arranging suitable coverage with correct policy ownership, payer and beneficiary structure at application; and coordinating the case with the attorney and accountant so the policy matches what the documents actually require. What does not belong to the agent: drafting or interpreting a buy-sell or any other agreement, opining on the tax treatment of premiums, benefits, entity structures or ownership arrangements, valuing the business, or advising on the corporate structure itself. The operating rule is that the agent asks for the professional determination in writing from the client's own advisers, records the referral and the answer received, and builds the case on what they supply rather than on an inference.

included: the need classes the agent may work with and quantify from adviser-supplied inputs
correct ownership, payer and beneficiary structuring at application
the written-referral rule and the record of the determination received
excluded: drafting, interpreting or opining on agreements, tax treatment, entity structure or business valuation
the case-level suitability recommendation and its documentation, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a client's agreements or adviser team change, or a recurring case class exceeds the practice's boundary

pros.claim: A clean boundary makes the agent a welcome participant on a professional team rather than a competitor to the client's other advisers
pros.example: an attorney who receives a precise coverage question and a written confirmation request begins referring insurance work back to the agent

cons.claim: Waiting on other professionals lengthens the sales cycle and can stall a case indefinitely when the client's advisers are slow or absent
cons.example: a case waits months for an attorney to confirm what an existing agreement actually requires before the amount can be finalized

failure_modes: answering a tax question conversationally because the answer seems obvious
arranging ownership or beneficiary structure from an assumption about an agreement nobody has read
letting the case proceed on a verbal characterization of a document that later turns out to be wrong
acceptance_tests: each business case file contains the adviser-supplied documents or figures the amount was built from, the written determination requested and received for any tax or legal question, and an ownership and beneficiary structure that matches what those sources state
revisit_triggers: the client's agreement, ownership or adviser team changes
a case class recurs that the practice cannot support within the boundary and must partner on or decline

nodes.definition: Choose lead sources that match the chosen market and the practice's real capacity, judging each class by its mechanics rather than its headline price. The classes: purchased direct-mail response leads, where the buyer has self-identified through a physical response device, intent is comparatively high, cost per lead is high, and the wording of the mail piece determines who responds; internet and shared leads, which arrive fast and cheap per unit, are frequently sold to several agents at once, and where speed to contact and the provenance of the consent record determine everything; telemarketed and transferred leads, which supply volume and where consent quality is the entire risk; seminars, workshops and worksite or association access, which build trust slowly and add venue, sponsor and content compliance obligations; personal network and community presence, which costs time rather than money; and referrals from existing clients and professional partners, which convert best of all. Each source is evaluated on cost per placed case rather than cost per lead, on whether its consent and do-not-call provenance can actually be evidenced on demand, and on whether its volume matches the number of appointments the practice can serve well - because a source that outruns capacity produces neglected prospects rather than sales.

included: the lead source classes and the mechanics that drive each one's quality
evaluation on cost per placed case and evidenced consent provenance
matching source volume to the practice's appointment capacity
excluded: the referral engine built on an in-force book with its cadence and life-event triggers, which belongs to the book building knowledge base
the sales conversation conducted once contact is made, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a source's measured cost per placed case drifts or a vendor changes its data sourcing or consent language

pros.claim: Measuring sources on cost per placed case rather than cost per lead reverses conclusions that per-lead pricing suggests
pros.example: an expensive direct-mail source with strong intent proves cheaper per placed case than a shared internet source sold to several agents simultaneously

cons.claim: Cost per placed case needs enough cases and enough elapsed time to be meaningful, so a source must be funded through a learning period before it can be judged
cons.example: a seminar channel is abandoned after one event, before the delayed appointments that make its economics work have had time to arrive

failure_modes: buying volume that exceeds the appointments the practice can actually keep, so paid leads decay unworked
using a source whose consent trail cannot be produced when a complaint arrives
judging a source on cost per lead and abandoning the one that actually places business
acceptance_tests: each active source has a vendor record naming its class, its consent and do-not-call provenance with the evidence retained, its measured cost per placed case, and the weekly volume the practice can serve
revisit_triggers: a source's measured cost per placed case drifts outside the modelled band
a vendor changes its data sourcing, consent language or exclusivity terms

nodes.definition: Every contact opens with an honest identification, and the marketing that produced the contact must be honest too. The rule set is short and absolute in its behaviour even where its legal specifics vary: identify yourself by name, state that you are a licensed insurance agent, and state that the purpose is to discuss life insurance, before anything else happens; never present the approach as a government program, a benefit entitlement, a survey, a claim, a service call on an existing policy, or an official notice; never use envelope, letterhead or caller-identification treatments designed to look like official mail, a government agency or a local acquaintance; honour do-not-call, consent and revocation obligation classes for calls, texts and emails, including the practice's own internal suppression list, and retain the evidence that consent existed for every purchased record; disclose the actual terms of any prize, giveaway or free-service inducement and check the anti-rebating and inducement rules of the state before offering one; and stop on request the first time it is made, permanently. The specifics of these classes differ by jurisdiction and channel and must be verified currently, but disclosure-first behaviour does not vary with the rules.

included: the disclosure-first opening used on every first contact
the prohibited framings, impersonations and mail or caller-identification treatments
consent, do-not-call, revocation, inducement and anti-rebating obligation classes with retained evidence
excluded: the specific do-not-call, consent and inducement rules of any jurisdiction or channel, which must be verified currently
the needs conversation that follows a compliant contact, which belongs to the needs analysis knowledge base

probabilistic_layer.update_signal: a complaint or consent dispute arises, or a jurisdiction changes contact and inducement rules

pros.claim: Opening with the truth costs some contacts and removes the entire class of complaints that begin with a prospect saying they were misled about why the agent called
